newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm with futures.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm with futures.

text.p: Med oil products were firmer on Tuesday as futures markets rose, traders said.
Gasoline markets were firmer with NYMEX futures. Offers of low octane material were still seen but buying was slack.
Naphtha was firmer with futures too. Skikda cargoes were heard offered into the Med at $5 over the quoted cif high cif Med, but few other barrels were avialable.
Dealers said high offers in NWE and across the Atlantic may attract cargoes from the mid east and possibly further afield.
Gas oil was slightly firmer but fairly quiet, with Greek and Turkish demand lending support to the market.
Two Russian cargoes were reported to be on offer. Traders assessed premiums at quotes cif high +$2.25/+$3.50 basis Genoa.

Traders submitted their offers for a Greek gas oil buy tender this morning. Participants quoted a premium range of quotes cif high to quotes cif high +$1.50, although none would give the exact level of their offers before awards are announced at the end of the week.
A Turkish tender for about 80,000 tonnes of October delivery gas oil closes on Wednesday.
Fuel oil prices retained their strength bolstered by tighness for good quality product.

Support was also expected from the winners of the latest Portuguese tender. "I wouldn't be surprised if some of the cargoes are sourced from the Med," said one trader. The tenders were understood to have been won with bids around mean fob Med +$10/10.25 delivered, but this was not confirmed.

Low sulphur cracked material was also underpinned by news that Turkey was looking for 45-50,000 tonnes during October and may possibly take more than one cargo. "I think demand has built up. Buyers have been very quiet over the last few weeks," said one trader.
